title: Rusty review pass 3: jmap-client
notes:
Targeted question answers:
1. |&s| s.to_owned() in request.rs:44 — IDIOMATIC. Correct pattern for converting &&str from .iter() into String.
2. b.is_ascii_hexdigit() in blob.rs:274 — FUNCTIONALLY CORRECT but contract mismatch with doc comment (see JMAP-he4.2). The predicate itself is idiomatic.
3. char::from(byte) in blob.rs:85 — CORRECT for ASCII-only branch (guard ensures byte < 128). char::from(u8) is defined for all u8; it's safe here. Slightly less idiomatic than char::from in hex_digit context (see JMAP-he4.4).
4. [(&str,&str);4] coercing to &[(&str,&str)] in blob.rs:208-216 — CORRECT. Array deref coercion to slice is idiomatic and compiles correctly.
5. Remaining .to_string() on literals — 3 in production code (JMAP-he4.1), several in tests (JMAP-he4.5).
6. New clippy issues from changes — 3 confirmed str_to_string violations (JMAP-he4.1). clippy passes clean at default lint level.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — The code is structurally sound and mostly idiomatic. The public API has one clear improvement opportunity (AuthProvider returning String instead of &str forces a clone on every request). The validate_sha256_format doc/predicate mismatch is a real P1 clarity issue. Three clippy str_to_string hits in production code are the most mechanical fix.
Rust idiom confidence: 85% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: JMAP-he4.3 (auth_header lifetime change is a public API break — may be intentionally deferred). Uncertainty driven by: did not see error.rs or push.rs; no visibility into whether ClientError derives are complete; could not run cargo check --all-features to verify feature-gated paths.
